name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.66.0 — `Depends on:` accepts a brief id with a trailing note (direct fix, core § Incident Policy): briefs spell dependencies as `16 (the review driver this brief mirrors)`; the item-wise parser rejected the item, so briefs 18, 19 and 23 silently carried no dependencies while status printed four remediation paragraphs for the tool's own strictness. spec-status.js now reads `NN`, `NN-name` or `brief NN` with one trailing parenthetical (commas inside it never split the item; header line breaks collapse); prose that is not an id still rejects and still surfaces as unparsed-dependency. Brief 24 (status-and-queue-diet) is staged for the shape that let this happen. tests/spec-status.test.js. 7.65.0 — replay-harness gaps surfaced by the first recorded replay miss (rp_0260cad37161, direct fix, core § Incident Policy): (1) `--setup --overlay` now materializes `.claude/agent-memory/` rows — worker notes are a build surface, not a review record — while the ledger, evidence, worktrees and rules under `.claude/` stay withheld; before, a host gate that sweeps those notes reddened the scratch tree on every replay for an edit the build had already made. (2) `--pick-class` skips the ids a host declares in `.claude/spec.config.json` → `replay.inapplicableClasses` (a class whose corpus section says "does not apply — pick another"), prints them as `skipped=`, refuses an id the corpus does not carry (exit 2, naming the valid ids) and refuses a list that rules out every class; this repo declares `server-code-in-client-bundle`. (3) The boundary-shift miss itself earns no guard: Incident Policy needs a third recurrence and the count is 1 — the ledger row is the record, a second miss of the class reopens the question. replay.md step 3 and Rules § Blindness, replay-corpus.md, tests/replay/replay.test.js. 7.64.0 — look stops are printed, never asked (direct fix, core § Incident Policy): the design stage's Step 5, /spec:sketch's ratification stop, and the /spec:mocks journey/review/approved marks print a fixed hand-off block — 🎨 the viewer command on its own line, 🆕 one component/screen name per line, `Reply ✅ approve — or — ✏️ change <notes>` — and end the turn; the user's reply is the decision. Before: the block was printed and then an `AskUserQuestion` was raised, and the terminal hides every line printed before a question dialog until it is answered while Ctrl-O dismisses it (claude-code #67475, #65392), so every design look since 7.57.1 made the user ask how to start the catalog and which components to check. Deep links, state lists, the 👀 gloss, and the gate-report line were cut from the block by user ruling (command + names only). New shared § Design Atlas rule `Look stops are never questions` (design.md doctrine, loaded by design/sketch/mocks/atlas/genesis); tests/design-look-handoff.test.js re-pinned across the three commands.
